text:
B: Hello. Jodie, is it?
A: Yeah, hiya. Sorry, I'm a bit frazzled, that's my fifth. Erm, you're Alison? With Biscuit?
B: The very same. He's had more mentions today than he's had walks this week.
A: Ha. Everyone's on about him. Do you know what this pays, by the way? I've asked literally everyone.
B: I think it's a voucher. Forty pounds? I didn't read it properly, which is very me.
A: Forty's alright. That's a week of chippy teas. So what do you do? I don't think anyone's said.
B: Planning, at the council. In Tonbridge.
A: Oh, so like, extensions and that?
B: Extensions, housing estates, the odd furious letter about a fence. Leanne wanted me to ban ugly shop signs, I had to disappoint her.
A: Ha, she would. I used to make them. Banners and signs, at a print firm in Wednesbury. Three years. Did anyone ever need permission for a banner?
B: Technically, sometimes. In practice, nobody asks and we don't chase them unless someone complains.
A: That's so much less exciting than I wanted it to be. Erm, I left anyway. I'm doing an MA now, in UX design, in Birmingham. Apps and websites.
B: Is that going well?
A: Erm. Honestly? I've had two extensions already and it's only March. I do everything the night before. And sometimes I think, like, I had a proper job, and I've packed it in and got a loan, and what if there's no jobs at the end of it? Sorry, that's a lot. Does that make sense?
B: It makes perfect sense. My daughter did something similar at about your age. Left a perfectly decent job, went back to study, panicked for a year.
A: And was it alright?
B: She's fine. Better than fine. She still panics, but now she gets paid for it.
A: Ha. That's the dream. You kind of remind me of my mum, by the way. Not in a bad way.
B: I'll take it. You've got a look of my daughter, actually. The clip. She wears her hair like that.
A: Does she tell you what you're doing wrong?
B: Constantly. Mostly my phone and my inbox. She's not wrong about the inbox.
A: My mum's on the family WhatsApp all day. It never stops. My nan sends voice notes, like, four minutes long, about the weather.
B: That's quite a skill, four minutes on weather.
A: She's got stamina. Sunday dinner at hers is the same. She doesn't stop talking or feeding you.
B: That sounds rather nice, to be honest.
A: It is, yeah. They just don't really get what I do. I'm the arty one, so I'm, like, "on the computer."
B: My family think I spend all day saying no to conservatories. Which isn't entirely untrue.
A: Ha. Are you doing anything nice after this?
B: Walking Biscuit, if it's not raining. Then dinner. Something out of the fridge, no recipe.
A: That's my nightmare, no recipe. I can do a chilli and fajitas and that's it.
B: That's two more than some people. Oh, that'll be the —
